observations.trace: Current embedded tiling and selected GPU/fitted producers form normal_deltas as target normals minus base normals. For a split edge, Split::push_vertex normalizes the linear interpolation of base normals but separately linearly interpolates each morph normal_delta. In ideal real arithmetic, consider two unit base normals A=(1,0,0), B=(0,1,0), two equal intended unit endpoint normals T=(0,0,1), and a non-endpoint split parameter t. The new base is normalize((1-t,t,0)); the interpolated delta is (-(1-t),-t,1). Their sum has positive x and y for 0<t<1 rather than the intended T, because the interpolated base has length less than one. The selected character finish retains the trimmed GeneratedArmor, armor_targets borrows its deltas, and the export source checks cardinality/finiteness then writes a NORMAL accessor.
observations.remaining: This refines Adler353 and original queue143, not a new unique historical defect. The example is symbolic only, with no normals, t, mesh, morph, export, renderer or test executed. Actual reachable geometry, endpoint and normalization policy, all producer/consumer variants and aliases remain open. Current trim fixture source uses a zero normal delta and cannot establish the nonzero curved case.

observations.trace: Trim::validate first rejects invalid width as a String then propagates Metal::validate and its Engraving::validate. Decoration::validate first validates its optional plate engraving, then optional trim. DecorationLibrary insert/load/save validates and maps the reason into anyhow context; selected Catalog article validation formats a decoration error with the item ID. Construction::trim_on may narrow a validated trim, and the selected worn-steel and armory sources pass it to armor_metal::trimmed.
observations.remaining: This reconnects original queue292 and delegate737, whose root adopter personally reread nothing. The trim width error is distinct from the Metal and Engraving first owners and from typed TrimError used at band geometry. Exact complete admission/caller paths and error/alias decisions remain open; no validation, file operation or caller ran.

observations.trace: The public GeneratedArmor::trimmed accepts a finite positive TrimBand.period. Rims::push_chain divides closed-rim length by that period, rounds periods and multiplies back to scale and closure. For a hypothetical finite unit square made from two outer triangles, the directed rim closes at length4. With period equal to the smallest positive normal binary32 value, 2^-126, ideal division yields 2^128, beyond finite binary32 maximum; under IEEE overflow to infinity, the subsequent scale/closure and first zero along coordinate may become nonfinite. The selected finish computes Trim.period as 1/(4*tiles); validated engraving tiles are bounded 0.25..64, giving period 1/256..1, with the no-engraving default inside that range.
observations.remaining: Adler353 identified the tiny-period standalone concern before this session; the unit-square source argument is new. No geometry, float operation, allocation, trim call or test ran. Compiler/target behavior, actual supported direct caller policy, producer frame bounds and downstream handling remain open. The bounded statement applies only to a validated Trim, not arbitrary public Trim values.

observations.trace: GeneratedArmor::trimmed checks finite positive band, prior trim, nonempty faces and three indices per face, before Rims consumes raw indices and positions. Split also indexes components and parallel attribute arrays. Current source tests assert a coarse square-band area bound and note corner overreach; the public documentation describes an exact width.
observations.remaining: The direct malformed-input contract, upstream producer guarantees, continuous geometric width and renderer quality are unresolved. The original reviewer already noted both limitations; no malformed armor, panic, geometry, preview or test was produced.
